newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE says Albania parties agree election deal.
newsitem.headline: OSCE says Albania parties agree election deal.

text.p: European envoy Franz Vranitzky said on Thursday that Albania's political parties had agreed to go ahead with a general election on June 29 in a deal thrashed out late on Wednesday.

"(Albanian) Prime Minister (Bashkim) Fino called me last night and he told me the political parties had agreed to solve the political situation in Albania...They have confirmed the election will be held on June 29," Vranitzky told a news conference.

Vranitzky, mediating in Albania for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) since widespread violence erupted in March, said the parties had agreed to elect 115 seats by majority voting and 40 seats through a proportional system.

"They also agreed on the makeup of central and regional electoral commissions and that all parties should have access to the media," the former Austrian chancellor said after addressing the OSCE's Vienna-based permanent council.
The 54-nation OSCE would give its total support to help in preparing the election and would send as many observers as was deemed necessary, together with the Council of Europe, Vranitzky said.
"We will help Albania. The whole international community is speaking with unanimity. There are no dissenting voices," he added.
